title: In January, British Muslims launched their own parliament, the Muslim Parliament of Great Britain, aiming to represent the interests of the two million Muslims in the UK. This initiative, led by Dr. Kalim Siddiqui of the Muslim Institute, follows 18 months of groundwork and is modeled after other religious institutions in the country. The inauguration took place on January 4 at Kensington Town Hall, where 155 Members of the Muslim Parliament (MMPs) were appointed, including 24 women. Although the parliament is still in its early stages, with plans for an Upper House in the future, it marks a significant step towards institutional representation for Muslims in Britain.
